method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that changes color.
questions.scope: Rapid camouflage and seasonal changes both count.

questions.prompt: Name a landform, natural feature or kind of landscape.
Name a percussion instrument.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
questions.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.

questions.prompt: Name a crime TV or streaming show.
Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
questions.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

questions.prompt: Name a champion in League of Legends.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name a stew or a named stew dish.
questions.scope: Named stews, braised one-pot dishes and recognized ingredient-based stew styles count. Soups that are also conventionally served as stews count; a raw ingredient, drink or dry standalone food does not.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Minnesota Timberwolves.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not.

questions.prompt: Name a food named after a place.
questions.scope: The place name must appear in an established food or dish name.

questions.prompt: Name a type of domestic animal.
Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument played by blowing air into it.
questions.scope: Mouth-blown instruments count, including reed, brass and free-reed instruments.

questions.prompt: Name a school or college from fiction.
questions.scope: Named fictional schools, colleges, universities and training academies count across books, TV, film, comics and games. A real school does not qualify just because a fictional story mentions it.

questions.prompt: Name a named weapon from a video game.
questions.scope: Unique named weapons and established weapon/item names count across all platforms.

questions.prompt: Name a pasta shape.
questions.scope: Named pasta shapes count; sauces and full dishes are separate.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name a type of boat, ship or other watercraft.
questions.scope: Kinds of boat, ship, raft or other vessel designed to travel on water or underwater count, past or present. Individual named vessels, wrecks, ice-only vehicles and descriptors of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a music act known as a duo.
questions.scope: Current and historical musical duos count. Ordinary backing musicians do not change a two-person act into a larger group. Two solo artists who collaborated once are not automatically a named duo.

questions.prompt: Name something you can wear that has a button, zipper or buckle.
questions.scope: Clothes, footwear, accessories and protective wear count.

questions.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
questions.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

questions.prompt: Name a type of paint.
questions.scope: Types of paint defined by medium, finish or purpose count, including artist and building paints. Color names alone, a layer of paint and digital painting software do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of parrot.
questions.scope: Parrot species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common and scientific names count. Pet colour mutations share their species identity; a bird is not a parrot just because its name contains that word.

questions.prompt: Name a real named dam.
questions.scope: Named real dams and barrages count, including historical dams and named projects already under construction. A reservoir name does not automatically name its dam, and fictional dams do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.

questions.prompt: Name a tool, instrument or piece of glassware used in a science laboratory.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with metal music.
Name a flower or flowering block found in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Flower items and blocks count, including tall flowers and Nether-compatible flowers. Named crops and saplings do not become flowers merely because they are plants. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of shop.
Name a character from SpongeBob SquarePants.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters from SpongeBob SquarePants, its films and spin-offs count. Identified character groups also count. Voice actors, episode titles and general species alone are not character names.

questions.prompt: Name a volcano or named volcanic complex. Dormant and extinct ones count.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a named pasta or noodle dish.
questions.scope: Named dishes and established menu preparations count, including familiar meal names such as spaghetti, udon and soba, filled pastas and gnocchi. A bare unfilled pasta-shape name without a dish or established menu preparation does not count. Plain tteokbokki is a rice-cake dish; rabokki includes noodles.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a web browser.
questions.scope: Actual web-browser products and families count, including historical, mobile and text browsers. A search engine, rendering engine, extension, website or operating system alone is not a browser.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Building”.
Name a kind of animal that can pollinate flowers.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Dua Lipa.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Dua Lipa count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a category of motor vehicle.
questions.scope: Types of self-propelled road or off-road vehicle count, with wheels, tracks or skids, including electric versions. Individual named models, rail vehicles, unpowered trailers and descriptions of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a comedy movie.
Name a sauce, condiment, or relish served with food. Named traditional condiments count.
Name a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
questions.scope: All base-game, Echo and DLC fighters count. Pokémon Trainer's three Pokémon, the three Mii fighting styles, and Pyra/Mythra count separately. Alternate costumes share the original fighter's answer; Assist Trophies do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of swallow or martin.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Hirundinidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a musician known for playing drums.
questions.scope: Real musicians known for playing drums count, including multi-instrumentalists and percussionists with a documented drum-playing career. An unrelated band member does not become a drummer just because the band has one.

questions.prompt: Name a real, named bridge.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a scientist, mathematician, inventor or science communicator.
Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a board or card game people can play together offline.
questions.scope: Published games and traditional named games count; video games do not.

questions.prompt: Name a real animal that has horns or antlers.
questions.scope: Living and extinct animals count, including beetle horns and other actual horn-like structures. Feathers that merely look like horns do not count. A named animal group counts when it contains horned or antlered members.

questions.prompt: Name an actor who appears in a Marvel Cinematic Universe movie.
questions.scope: Released MCU feature films count; voice and motion-capture performances count too.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a river, lake, sea, ocean, gulf, bay or strait.
Name a type of musical instrument. Named instrument families count.
Name an audio listening, recording or amplification device.
questions.scope: Physical devices for listening to, picking up, recording, reproducing or amplifying audio count. Musical instruments by themselves, warning bells and noise-suppression-only devices do not.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Survival”.
Name a kind of marsupial. Named groups and species, living or extinct, count; a common or scientific name is accepted.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a current MLB team (2026).
Name an action movie.
Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name a type of chair or stool.
questions.scope: Recognizable chair and seated-stool designs count, past or present. Benches, couches, named individual thrones and the person chairing a meeting do not.

questions.prompt: Name a named object in our Solar System.
questions.scope: Planets, dwarf planets, moons, named asteroids and named comets count; stars beyond the Sun do not.

questions.prompt: Name a country whose national flag contains a star.
questions.scope: A visible star on the official national flag qualifies; tiny stars inside a coat of arms count too.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of shark or ray.
questions.scope: Established groups and species count; familiar common names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of equipment an athlete wears.
questions.scope: Protective gear, specialist footwear and worn sporting equipment count; handheld equipment does not.

questions.prompt: Name an emote from Fortnite.
questions.scope: Any recorded season or collaboration counts. These are cosmetic names, not Battle Royale weapon names.

questions.prompt: Name a named salad or established salad variety.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of equipment used to take or process photographs.
questions.scope: Physical equipment, supplies and accessories used in still photography count, including darkroom materials. A finished photograph, filmed sequence or a device used only to mark a film take does not.

questions.prompt: Name a musical artist or band with a number in their name.
questions.scope: Numbers written as digits, words or Roman numerals count.

questions.prompt: Name a bird that cannot normally fly, including extinct flightless birds.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a real named beach.
questions.scope: Real named coastal, lake and river beaches count. A city name qualifies when it is also the established name of a beach. A whole country, waterbody or general tourist region alone does not name a beach.

questions.prompt: Name an item or block a furnace recipe can produce in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Give the output, rather than the input, of an ordinary furnace smelting or cooking recipe. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a gesture or bodily signal.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional detective.
questions.scope: Named fictional professional detectives and amateur sleuths count across books, comics, film, TV and games. A character must actually investigate cases; merely appearing in a mystery does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a real mountain, mountain peak or volcano.
questions.scope: Named mountains, mountain peaks and volcanoes on Earth count. Whole mountain ranges, unnamed coordinates, fictional mountains and names only found on other planets are outside this inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of owl.
questions.scope: Owl species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common names and scientific names count. An owlet-nightjar or a nighthawk is not an owl.

questions.prompt: Name a playable hero in Overwatch.
questions.scope: The full official Overwatch roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts, including heroes introduced while it was called Overwatch 2. Skins and unplayable story characters do not.

questions.prompt: Name a quarterback who started and won a Super Bowl.
questions.scope: The quarterback must have started a winning Super Bowl, through Super Bowl LX in February 2026. Winning a ring as a backup alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name an anime TV or streaming show.
Name a sushi style or named sushi roll.
questions.scope: Established sushi preparations, named sushi rolls and recognizable filling-specific sushi varieties count. Sashimi by itself is not sushi because it lacks the seasoned rice. A fish or ingredient alone is not a prepared sushi variety.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Foo Fighters.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Foo Fighters count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a machine or device that uses an electric motor.
questions.scope: The motor can be internal and does not need to move the entire device.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a spoken, signed or constructed language.
Name a motorsport or established motor-racing series.
questions.scope: Recognized motor-vehicle competitions and racing series count, including cars, motorcycles, boats, snowmobiles and powered aircraft. Drivers, vehicle manufacturers and unpowered sports do not qualify by themselves.

questions.prompt: Name a science fiction movie.
Name an everyday object with wheels.
questions.scope: Ordinary objects and vehicles count; named types count without needing a brand.

questions.prompt: Name a named type of bread.
questions.scope: Named breads, rolls and flatbreads count; filling-only variations do not create a new bread.

questions.prompt: Name a gas or common gas mixture.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a cat breed, including experimental and historical breeds.
Name a game on Steam tagged “Fighting”.
Name a song by Twenty One Pilots.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Twenty One Pilots count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Utah Jazz.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. New Orleans Jazz seasons also count.

questions.prompt: Name a character from Shrek or Puss in Boots.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters in the Shrek films and spin-offs, including Puss in Boots films, count. Identified groups such as the Three Little Pigs count. Voice actors and generic fairy-tale species alone do not count.
